fixes.explanation: Not this time, friend. Ziba's cargo in this verse is donkeys, bread, raisins, summer fruit and wine, with no weapons mentioned. Armed men aren't part of what he brings. Ziba came to the road carrying groceries, not swords.

Yes, baker. Ziba says, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat…” He adds that the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness. Donkeys for riding, food for eating, wine for the worn out. I can't even explain my own cookie budget that clearly.

Good guess, but no prophet in this answer. Ziba says the donkeys are for the king's household to ride, and the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat. The word is king. A prophet would have to wait his turn, and apparently he wasn't even in line.

Right, baker. David asks where Mephibosheth is, and Ziba answers that he is staying in Jerusalem. Then Ziba reports that Mephibosheth has said, “Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.” Notice that this is what Ziba says Mephibosheth said.

Not what the text says, baker. David doesn't send Ziba anywhere in these verses. He says, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” That's no palace watch, just a whole lot of property changing hands on a dusty road.

That one belongs to Ziba, friend, and even he didn't ask for mercy. Ziba said, “I humbly bow before you,” and asked to find favor in the king's eyes. Shimei came out of Bahurim with a very different style. He kept yelling out curses and threw stones.

Right, baker. David says, “If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’…” He doesn't answer Shimei with a fight. He says "if," and leaves room for the LORD to be behind it. That's a lot to say with stones flying at him.
